metaDescription: F1, Tropicana chinese cabbage is a chinese cabbage variety. 58 to 62 days to harvest, 11.1 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: F1, Tropicana is a registered chinese cabbage variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. Takii bred it. It takes 58 to 62 days from transplanting to harvest, with 11.13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 58 to 62 days from transplanting to harvest.
**Yield:** 11.13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about F1, Tropicana chinese cabbage
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

F1, Tropicana chinese cabbage takes 58 to 62 days from transplanting to harvest. That is about the average of the 4 chinese cabbage varieties with a day count, 57.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 11.13 t/ha trails the average of its group, 12.68. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chinese cabbage fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant F1, Tropicana chinese cabbage

Pechay Baguio heads best in cool places. In the lowlands, pick a heat tolerant hybrid and plant in the cool months. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 58 to 62 days from transplanting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 11.13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of F1, Tropicana?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
